newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee stays lower by close, trade sluggish.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee stays lower by close, trade sluggish.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures stayed lower by the close on Tuesday in a sluggish session with the market seemed heading for a bout of familiar range trading.
"It's a pretty miserable day," said one trader. "There was no fresh news and the only real feature was the May/July switch."

Market turnover reached a paltry 2,333 lots, with less than 700 lots seen in the morning trade. Traders said much of the trade interest was diverted to cocoa market which regained lustre this week after Monday's heavy fund-led selling.
Benchmark May closed $5 down at $1,570 a tonne after trading between $1,567 and $1,581. Traders said the market's upside potential is now limited with volume and volatility fast dwindling.
"This could point to a lower level in the short-term," said one.
May/July spread narrowed to $6 by the close from $10 on Monday.
The New York arabica futures also failed to shine, fluctuating narrowly in either direction.
Coffee came under heavy fund sell-off last week. The funds' flight out of commodities has now hit cocoa and base metals.
"The funds are liquidating in commodities in general," said a trader.
But there were no fresh fund sales seen in coffee this week and traders viewed this as constructive to the market.
On the other hand, industry buying remained slow while origin sellers were scarce amid lower prices.
Roasters, returning from Easter break, were still taking stock of the situation after the heavy purchases in January and February and were reluctant to commit.
Some European manufacturers were also seen well covered until June.
Options saw some 1,100 lots changing hands this morning with the May $1,650 and $1,700 calls and July $1,100 and $1,200 puts leading the actives.
July $1,200 put saw a volatility of 42 percent and $1,100 at 48 percent but traders said the premium was small and insignificant.
Traders said the options activity was dominated by book squaring ahead of the May expiry.

In other news, Tanzania's northern arabica coffee output could fall to as low as 10,000 tonnes for the 1997/98 season because of severe drought which hit much of East Africa, government and industry officials said.
The production totalled about 16,000 tonnes in 1996/97.
